Lessons begin with the home keys for the left hand: 'ASDF'.  Place the little finger over the 'A' key; ring finger over 'S'; middle finger over 'D'; and index finger over 'F'.  Keep the fingers curved, relaxed and poised just over the home keys.
Keypad entries are made with the right hand.  The home keys are: '456'.  The index finger is used on the '4' key; middle finger on '5'; and ring finger on '6'.  The '+' key acts as an Enter key.
There are six menus in this program: the Main Menu and the secondary menus of Lessons, Tests, Reports, Options, and Game.  The top line on each menu shows the available menu features.
The second line gives more information about the highlighted feature.

To select a feature use the right and left arrow keys (or the space bar) to highlight it.  When the feature you want is highlighted, press Enter to select it.  You can also make a selection by typing the first letter of the desired feature.
If the highlighted item is the name of a secondary menu, the second line shows that menu's available features.  Otherwise, the second line describes the highlighted feature.
Use your %s %s finger to strike both the '%c' and '%c' keys.
Type the line in the top box.  The arrow moves to show the next key to type.  At the end of the line press either space bar or Enter.

So far, lessons have used lower case characters only.  New lessons will use upper case letters as well.  Upper case letters are typed by holding down a Shift key at the same time the letter is pressed.
There are two Shift keys, one for each hand.  Hold the Shift key down with the little finger of one hand and type the letter with the correct finger on the other hand.

For example, to type an upper case 'E', press the Shift key on the right side of the keyboard with the right little finger.  While holding the Shift key down, press the 'E' key with the left middle finger.

Appended overlay bytes are identified by file extent and included in FileBytes identity; they must not be mapped as initialized header/module memory. Uninitialized allocations are reported but their contents and DOS runtime behavior are not verified.
The fixed load segment 0x1000 describes Ghidra's analysis image, not a running DOS process. Verified import does not establish original source ownership or recovered program behavior.
A mismatching memory digest identifies the reported source range; it does not locate the first differing byte inside that range.
